seo.title: etcd GUI for {devices}
seo.description: Browse etcd keys by prefix, change values and leases in a grid, and run etcdctl-style get, put, watch and lease commands, with TLS and SSH tunnels.

header.title: etcd GUI
header.lead: Browse etcd keys by prefix, change values and leases in a grid, and run etcdctl-style commands.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter one host and its client port; the peer port has no JSON gateway, and there is no database selection or endpoint failover. Leave Username and Password empty on a cluster without authentication. A user without the root role browses the keys its roles cover, while endpoint status and the user and role commands answer permission denied.

TLS is set by TLS Mode in the Advanced fields and starts Disabled. Required (skip verify) encrypts without checking, Verify CA checks the certificate against the CA file you name, and Verify Identity adds the hostname; a client certificate and key add mutual TLS. etcd:// and etcds:// URLs import, and neither switches TLS on by itself.

bands.title: Browse keys and run commands
text: Set Key Prefix Root, such as /app, to scope a connection to one subtree. The sidebar groups keys by their first path segment under it, and each key is a row with its value, version, mod and create revisions, and lease.

Saving an edit sends commands: a new value or lease puts the key again, a NULL lease removes the lease, and a rename puts the new name and deletes the old one. The revision columns belong to etcd, so an edit to one stops the save and names the column.

Run etcdctl-style key, watch, lease, member, endpoint, compaction and access-control commands with command and flag completion; unsupported ones are rejected before they reach the server. Safe Mode runs get, watch and the commands that only list or report as reads, and counts every other command as a write.

bands.title: Leases and the cluster
text: Manage leases and revision compaction from the editor, and inspect members and endpoint status or health with commands. Running auth enable turns authentication on for the whole cluster: a connection that holds a username and password keeps working, and one that holds neither has to be reopened with credentials.

moveData: <export>Export</export> keys or a command’s result as {exportFormats}.

faq.question: Why does a lease ID point at a different lease?
faq.answer: Lease IDs take decimal or hex, and hex is recognised by its letters. Prefix an all-digit hex ID with 0x, as in --lease=0x69407712, or it reads as decimal and resolves to another lease.

faq.question: Can I edit binary values?
faq.answer: No. A value that is not valid UTF-8 shows in the grid as its base64, marked as such, and text you type is sent as UTF-8. Write binary values with etcdctl.
